basis: Assumption: a braking corner with apex >= 200 km/h counts as one fast-corner equivalent. Downforce grows with speed squared, so the aero grip a car loses in the wake matters most here
Assumption: a braking corner with apex 120-200 km/h counts half a fast corner. Speed squared at a typical 160 vs 230 km/h apex is about 0.48 of the fast value

Assumption: a braking corner with apex < 120 km/h counts a quarter. Speed squared alone gives about 0.15; raised because the car spends longer in a slow corner and the wake still costs some front grip on entry. Being held up is NOT included

Assumption: a kink taken flat (fewer than half of clear-air passes brake) is not grip-limited in clean air, so the wake costs little there; a small allowance equal to a slow corner for the lift a following car may need. Tow gain is NOT included
Assumption: with 2017-18 cars, a full lap within 1 s of the car ahead on a reference lap costs 0.35 s (mid-to-upper end of the few-tenths range commonly reported for following closely)
The reference lap: 8 fast-corner equivalents, about a typical circuit on this scale (median over the 2018-25 races is 6.75; Silverstone 9.4, Monza 5.0)
Floor: no race is assumed to cost less than 0.15 s for a full lap within 1 s. Binds only for low-index circuits in 2022 (Monza, Red Bull Ring, Paul Ricard, Yas Marina); flagged loss_bounded
Ceiling: no race is assumed to cost more than 0.55 s for a full lap within 1 s (above the top of the few-tenths range). Does not bind on 2018-25 data; flagged loss_bounded if it ever does
Era factor 1.00 (reference). 2017 rules made cars wider with much more downforce, and following became markedly harder; the 2017-18 car is the reference this scale is set on

Era factor 0.90. The 2019 rules simplified front wings and bargeboard-area devices specifically to reduce the wake's effect on a following car, and the 2021 floor trim cut downforce further. Reported gain was modest, so only 10% off

Era factor 0.65. The 2022 ground-effect rules were designed for following: F1's published CFD put the downforce loss at about 1 car length near 18% (vs about 47% for 2021 cars). Drivers reported a real but smaller gain than the CFD, so 0.65 and not 0.4
Era factor 0.75. In 2023 teams regained outwash (floor edges, front wing endplates) and the floor rules were raised 15 mm; drivers widely reported following got harder again than in 2022
Era factor 0.80. Mature ground-effect cars: drivers reported following harder than in 2022-23 but still easier than before 2022
NOT ASSESSED: 2026 brings new rules (smaller, lighter cars with active aero) and there is no evidence yet on following. Carries the 2024-25 factor forward and flags era_assessed = false
Neutral multiplier used when a lap has no compound, an unresolved compound, no constructor, or no constructor row. The lap is flagged (factor_flag), never silently defaulted
